requirements.source: harness-console journeys preamble; VISION ("on a laptop or a phone").

requirements.title: Live without reload
requirements.statement:
Views update from the event stream, falling back to polling. A stale or disconnected view says
so.
acceptance: AC1: Killing the stream connection shows a "reconnecting" state and recovers without a reload.
requirements.source: harness-console J1; decided D5; console `lib/live.ts`.

requirements.title: Command palette
requirements.statement: A keyboard palette jumps to any task, chain or run by id or text and runs common actions.
acceptance: AC1: Typing `ROVE-12` and Enter opens that task from any page.
requirements.source: harness-console J2 ("⌘K palette jumps to any request/chain/run by id"); console `command-palette` component.

requirements.title: Design tokens and brand
requirements.statement: One token set (colour, type, spacing) with light and dark themes, using the Sortyard brand kit.
acceptance: AC1: No component hard-codes a colour.
requirements.source: meta-harness `projects/sortyard/branding/`; harness-console decided D3.

requirements.title: Empty, error and unknown states are designed
requirements.statement:
Every view has a designed state for: nothing yet, loading, failed to load, and value unknown.
An absent value is never rendered as zero, a blank or a spinner that never ends.
acceptance: AC1: Storybook (or equivalent) has a story per state per view, and the e2e suite visits the failed and unknown states.
requirements.source: AGENTS.md "Testing model" (one story per machine state; every gate defines its absent state); harness-console J1.

requirements.title: Strings are externalised; English only
requirements.statement:
All user-visible strings go through a message catalogue with locale-aware dates and numbers.
1.0 ships English only and documents how a locale is added.
acceptance: AC1: A lint fails on a hard-coded user-visible string in a component.
AC2: A pseudo-locale build renders every route without clipped or missing text.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark (22 locales, an i18n sync check in CI); see [12-quality-bar.md](12-quality-bar.md) for the stance.

requirements.title: Embedded concierge
requirements.statement:
The embedded chat agent of the existing console (ask a question, get an answer grounded in live
state with citations, approve proposed actions) is not part of 1.0. Its ambient half — the
attention list — is (OBS-014). Operators reach the same capability from their own agent through
MCP.
acceptance: AC1: The read tools the concierge used are present in the operator-agent MCP set (MCP-002), so the feature can return without new API work.
requirements.source: harness-console J6–J8, decided D7–D9, D14–D15; console `components/concierge/*`. Owner decision OD-3.

requirements.title: One ordered ledger, written with the state it describes
requirements.statement:
Every state change writes one event `{seq, time, actor, object, transition, facts, refs}` in the
same database transaction as the change. Events are append-only and globally ordered by `seq`.
Scheduling decisions and audit entries are event classes in the same order, so one task's
timeline interleaves all three.
acceptance: AC1: There is no code path that changes a state table without an event (enforced by routing all writes through domain commands and a test that diffs tables against events after the scenario suite).
AC2: Appending the same event twice records it once; reusing an id for different content is refused.
AC3: Update, delete and truncate on ledger tables are refused by the database.
requirements.source: migration `0001` (append-only triggers, `append_event` idempotency); DESIGN §3.8; FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN ("A durable event ledger is the follow-up for exact historical series").

requirements.title: History of any object
requirements.statement: For any object the API returns its events in order, with who, when, before and after.
acceptance: AC1: The current state of a task equals the fold of its events (replay test).
requirements.source: `sortyard.object_history(kind, id)`; harness-console J5.

requirements.title: Read models are projections and say so
requirements.statement:
Aggregates (queue census, throughput windows, dashboards) are computed from the ledger and
state tables, are recomputable at will, store nothing authoritative, and are labelled with
`as_of`. A read model never feeds a scheduling decision.
acceptance: AC1: Dropping and rebuilding every read model changes no API result other than `as_of`.
AC2: A read endpoint causes no write, no Job and no outbound call.
requirements.source: FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN ("The read model is a projection of source records, never a second authority"; "No request body, database write, Job creation, or trace span is caused by these reads").

requirements.title: The metric catalogue
requirements.statement:
Sortyard ships one catalogue in which each metric has an id, an exact definition (numerator,
denominator, clock, window, cohort), a unit and its coverage rule. The v1 catalogue:

| Id | Definition |
|---|---|
| `queue.actionable` | Eligible tasks and admissible stages now, by project and state. Age runs from the release or queued transition to first schedule; open waits use `as_of`. |
| `stage.pickup_latency` | For stages first scheduled in the window: `first_scheduled − eligible_since`, where `eligible_since` is the later of the queued transition and the predecessor's pass. Dependency wait is reported separately and is never called a scheduler delay. |
| `stage.execution` | For attempts terminal in the window: scheduled→running, running→collecting, collecting→terminal. Missing endpoints are counted, not dropped. |
| `chain.outcomes` | Chains that reached a terminal outcome in the window, once each, by outcome (done, parked, handed-back, cancelled), with shares. |
| `chain.cycle_time` | For chains done in the window: done − claimed. Open chains are shown by current age, not included in percentiles. |
| `task.lead_time` | For tasks done in the window: done − created; and time in each board state. |
| `merges` | Change requests merged into a default branch in the window, by host merge time, unique by repo and number. |
| `merge.open_to_first_green` / `merge.green_to_merge` / `merge.open_to_merge` | From the change request's history and its required check runs. |
| `review.rounds` | Reviews with a verdict per task; share of tasks at or over the tripwire. |
| `fix.rounds`, `conflict.rounds` | Per task and per window. |
| `lanes.utilisation` | Slot-seconds held ÷ slot-seconds available, by project; same for each heavy cap. |
| `handback.count`, `park.count` | By reason and blocking-cause kind. |
| `cost.agent_minutes_per_merge` | Agent wall time of every finished stage for a project (builds, reviews, fix rounds, triage, failures) ÷ changes merged in its repos, same window. |
| `cost.stages_per_merge`, `cost.tokens_per_merge` | Same cohort; tokens where recorded. |
| `main.health` | Per repo: latest completed required run on the default branch, its conclusion, and the age of the last success. |
acceptance: AC1: Each metric has a fixture with a hand-computed expected value.
AC2: A metric whose source is incomplete returns `null` with a reason (API-012).
AC3: Percentiles use nearest-rank and state `n`.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract "Metric definitions"; `metrics/analyze.py` (merged per day, open→first green, last green→merge, open→merge, review rounds, auto-merge use); conductor README `cost_item`.

requirements.title: Throughput windows
requirements.statement:
Catalogue metrics are available per hour, day and week, by project, lane and workflow. Windows
describe the past and gate nothing.
acceptance: AC1: Window boundaries are half-open and in UTC; a record is counted in exactly one window.
requirements.source: DESIGN §3.8 ThroughputWindow; Joe 2026-11-05 (time survives only as looking back at throughput).

requirements.title: Delivery cost
requirements.statement:
For each project and window: agent-minutes per merged change and stages per merged change,
computed from recorded stage usage. Stages whose usage is unreadable are named, not guessed.
acceptance: AC1: The published number and the list of excluded stages always appear together.
requirements.source: driver §3 "Delivery cost" (k3s-harness #186: "Unreadable requests are named, not guessed").

requirements.title: Wait versus work
requirements.statement:
For any chain and any window the time is decomposed into: waiting on dependencies, waiting for a
slot, waiting for admission, executing, waiting on CI, waiting on review, waiting on a person.
acceptance: AC1: The components sum to the cycle time within one second.
AC2: Each component maps to reason codes (SCH-009), so the dashboard and the Pickup Preview agree.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract ("Stage timing waterfall and wait-vs-execution decomposition"); FACTORY-STAGE-ATTEMPTS-DESIGN.

requirements.title: Queue census
requirements.statement:
A cheap, bounded endpoint returns current counts: eligible, held by reason, claimed by phase,
stages queued, running and collecting, slots and caps in use. Downstream stages of an open chain
are future work, not queue depth.
acceptance: AC1: The census never counts a stage under a terminal chain as runnable.
requirements.source: `GET /api/mh/queue-census`; FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN (`eligible_queued_stages` rule).

requirements.title: Daily record
requirements.statement:
One generated record per day and project: what merged, what did not and why, what is parked or
handed back, incidents on main, quarantined jobs, cost. Generated from the ledger; nobody writes
it by hand.
acceptance: AC1: The record for a past day is reproducible byte for byte.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 view 13 ("no hand-written status ever again"); JOB-QUARANTINE.md (`ledger/pipeline-daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md`).

requirements.title: System metrics endpoint
requirements.statement:
Each component serves Prometheus metrics: reconcile duration and lag, claim latency, queue
depth, Job counts by phase, API latency and error rate, database pool use, mirror age, ledger
append rate.
acceptance: AC1: The metric names and labels are documented and covered by a snapshot test.
AC2: Scraping needs no credential beyond network reach, or a token when configured.
requirements.source: inference — the legacy system exposes `/api/health` and OTLP only; the standard for Kubernetes installs is a scrape endpoint.

requirements.title: Structured logs with correlation ids
requirements.statement:
Logs are JSON lines with level, component, request id and — where they apply — project, task,
chain, stage and attempt.
acceptance: AC1: One `grep` by a correlation id — request or task id in MS1, chain id from MS3 — across component logs yields the whole story.
AC2: Error output from child processes is captured, not discarded.
requirements.source: 2026-11-12 release stall ("stderr is discarded, so it was reproduced with a server-side dry run").

requirements.title: OpenTelemetry export
requirements.statement:
Optional export of lifecycle spans over OTLP, with W3C trace context carried from task to chain
to stage. Export uses an outbox with a bounded backlog; drops are counted and reported. The
ledger stays the record: telemetry never overwrites state.
acceptance: AC1: With the collector down, nothing blocks and the gap is visible in health.
requirements.source: `mh.py` trace outbox (notes: trim pending over 5,000, prune delivered after 7 days); OTLP-TRACE-DESIGN; factory-measurement-contract ("Never overwrite authoritative business state with telemetry").

requirements.title: Notifications
requirements.statement:
Routing rules send events to channels (webhook, Slack-compatible webhook, email). Shipped
defaults notify a person only for owner-list items (REC-024) and for a factory-down state with
nothing acting on it. Everything else goes to the pipeline: a task, a condition, a queue.
Notifications are de-duplicated per condition and their delivery is logged.
acceptance: AC1: A red main with an active triage chain sends no notification.
AC2: A notification that could not be delivered is itself a condition after its retry budget.
requirements.source: driver §6 ("Findings go to the pipeline, not to the owner … The stall watch stays quiet about a red that has an active conductor item"); DV40-ALERT-READBACK-DESIGN.

requirements.title: Attention list
requirements.statement:
A computed list of what needs a look now: chains past their phase bound, credentials expiring or
quarantined, red main with nothing acting, silent mechanisms, low quota, open conditions. Each
entry carries its evidence links. An entry can be dismissed with a reason and restored.
acceptance: AC1: The list is the same through API, MCP (`get_attention`) and UI.
AC2: Dismissal is audited and expires when the underlying condition changes.
requirements.source: harness-console J8; API.md "Needs-attention insights (HC-14)"; console calls `/api/insights`, `/dismiss`, `/restore`.

requirements.title: No phone-home
requirements.statement:
Sortyard sends nothing to its authors or any third party. There is no usage telemetry in 1.0;
any later telemetry is opt-in and documented field by field.
acceptance: AC1: A network-policy test runs the full scenario suite with egress limited to the configured Git host and model provider.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark (instance telemetry defaults to enabled).

requirements.title: Retention
requirements.statement:
Retention is configuration with documented defaults: ledger events (keep), traces and stage
logs (90 days), run directories (REC-022), webhook delivery logs (30 days). Expiry is a
registered mechanism.
acceptance: AC1: Expired blobs are removed and their references say "expired", not "missing".
requirements.source: `mh.py` retention (notes); DESIGN §3.6 `retention` policy kind (parameters left open in the frozen schema).

requirements.title: Main-branch release health
requirements.statement:
Per repo: the latest completed required run on the default branch and the age of the last
success. A failing required run is a factory-down signal until a later success; an owner-accepted
hold changes its disposition, not its colour.
acceptance: AC1: Green change-request checks never dilute this state.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract "Mainline release health".

requirements.title: Improvement ledger
requirements.statement:
A record per tuning intervention with hypothesis, pre and post cohort values and a verdict
(`improved`, `regressed`, `inconclusive`, `not_live`).
acceptance: AC1: Until it ships, the audit of policy changes (SCH-011) plus the windowed metrics give the raw material.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract "Sense → respond → improve loop".

requirements.title: A small set of definition kinds, all versioned
requirements.statement:
Definitions in 1.0: `policy` (rules and thresholds), `lane` settings, `project` configuration,
`workflow`, `packet-template`, `harness-profile`, `checklist`. Each version is immutable and
content-hashed; the newest valid version is current. Policies, lanes and project configuration
arrive in MS2; the rest in MS3.
acceptance: AC1: Editing a definition creates a new version; an existing version can never change (database-enforced).
AC2: Applying identical content twice creates no new version.
AC3: Archetypes, context recipes, roles, skills and eval packs are not definition kinds in 1.0 (CF-05).
requirements.source: `definitions/README.md` (immutable content-hashed versions); DESIGN §5.1; CF-05 for the cut.

requirements.title: The database is authoritative; files are how definitions travel
requirements.statement:
All definitions live in the database. `sortyardctl apply -f <dir|file|git-url@ref>` creates
versions from files through the API; `sortyardctl export` writes the current versions as files.
Export then apply is a no-op. There is no sync controller and no "definitions: stale" state.
acceptance: AC1: Round-trip test: export → apply on a second install yields identical content hashes.
AC2: A UI edit and an `apply` of the same content produce the same version.
requirements.source: DESIGN §5.1 (git and database both, with a sync controller); CF-06 for why this is changed. Owner decision OD-5.

requirements.title: Source lock
requirements.statement:
An installation can lock definitions to a source: only `apply` from the configured repository
and ref (run by a token with the `definitions-source` role, typically from CI) may create
versions; the UI shows definitions read-only and links to the source.
acceptance: AC1: With the lock on, a UI or API edit by an operator is refused with a message naming the source.
AC2: The NonceLogic installation runs locked, which keeps "definition edits go through git review".
requirements.source: INTENDED-USE.md standing default ("definition edits via git PRs").

requirements.title: A running chain keeps the versions it started with
requirements.statement:
A chain pins its workflow, packet-template and checklist versions at claim. New versions apply
to new chains. Policy thresholds, by contrast, are read at decision time.
acceptance: AC1: Editing a workflow mid-chain changes nothing for that chain.
AC2: The task detail shows the pinned versions.
requirements.source: DESIGN §5.1 (a) "pinning wins"; DESIGN §3.6 (policies read at decision time).

requirements.title: Every legacy constant is a named policy key with a documented default
requirements.statement:
No tunable is a literal in code. The table below is the starting key set; each row ships in the
milestone that introduces its behaviour, and a test asserts the code reads the key.

| Legacy constant | Value today | Policy key |
|---|---|---|
| `lanes` per project | 3 / 3 / 2 / 1 … | `project.lanes` |
| `MH_HEAVY_CAP` / `MH_TRAIN_HEAVY_CAP` / `MH_PROJECT_HEAVY_CAP` | 4–6 / 3–5 / 2 (deployment-specific) | `admission.heavy_cap`, `.train_cap`, `.project_heavy_cap` |
| stage deadlines | 45 / 60 / 60 / 120 min; max 3 h | `stage.<class>.deadline_seconds` |
| `BUILD_DEADLINE_S` | 3 h | `workflow.change.build_deadline_seconds` |
| `FIX_ROUNDS` | 10 (backstop) | `fix.backstop_rounds` |
| `CONFLICT_ROUNDS` | 5 | `fix.conflict_rounds` |
| `REVIEW_TRIPWIRE` | 5 | `review.tripwire` |
| `INFRA_RETRIES` / `INFRA_WAIT` / `INFRA_WAITS` | 3 / 30 min / 2 | `infra.retries`, `.wait_seconds`, `.waits` |
| consecutive step errors | 5 | `infra.consecutive_errors` |
| cluster-API retries | 6 | `infra.cluster_api_retries` |
| `API_WAIT` | 90 s | `infra.dependency_wait_seconds` |
| `STALL` | 4 h | `stall.phase_seconds` |
| `CHECKS_GRACE` | 30 min | `merge.missing_check_grace_seconds` |
| `TRIAGE_TRIES` / `TRIAGE_ROUNDS` | 3 / 2 | `triage.attempts`, `triage.merged_fix_rounds` |
| `DISPATCH_GRACE` / `PROOF_WAIT` / `CONFIRM_LIMIT` | 20 min / 3 h / 24 h | `triage.dispatch_grace_seconds`, `.run_wait_seconds`, `.confirm_limit_seconds` |
| causes `POLL` / `RETURNS` | 30 min / 2 | `causes.poll_seconds`, `causes.infra_returns` |
| self-heal drain | 24 h | `selfheal.stalled_after_seconds` |
| grooming alarm | 2 failures / 60 min | `grooming.failed_attempts`, `grooming.empty_queue_seconds` |
| filing sweep | 30 min | `filing.will_release_limit_seconds` |
| `QUEUED_AFTER` | 30 min | `ci.unrunnable_after_seconds` |
| job quarantine exit | 7 days / 20 clean runs | `quarantine.max_days`, `quarantine.clean_runs` |
| `MAX_SURFACES` | 8 | `preflight.max_surfaces` |
| test review deadlines | 10 / 15 min | `review.test.execution_seconds`, `.outer_seconds` |
| design review deadlines | 20 / 30 min | `review.design.execution_seconds`, `.outer_seconds` |
| pool window / cooling / requeues | 5 h / 5 h / 3 | `pool.usage_window_seconds`, `.cooling_seconds`, `.limit_requeues` |
| pool probe interval / deadline | 15 min / 900 s | `pool.probe_interval_seconds`, `.probe_deadline_seconds` |
| CLI soak | 6 h | `harness.cli_soak_hours` |
| packet cap | 200,000 chars | `packet.max_chars` |
| run retention / pressure | 24 h / 85% / 4 h | `retention.run_seconds`, `.pressure_percent`, `.pressure_seconds` |
| mirror freshness | 300 s | `mirror.stale_after_seconds` |
| mechanism check cadence / quota floor | 10 min / 20% | `health.check_seconds`, `quota.low_fraction` |

acceptance: AC1: The policy reference page is generated from the key registry and shows key, default, legacy name and the requirement that uses it.
AC2: A key with no reader, or a reader of an unregistered key, fails CI.
requirements.source: `drive.py` constants and their notes; `mh.py` constants (notes); conductor README; MECHANISMS.md; DESIGN §5.3 ("If a knob exists in code as a literal, that's a bug against this design").

requirements.title: Definitions are validated when applied
requirements.statement:
`apply` validates schema and meaning and refuses with a message naming the definition and the
rule: an unbounded phase (REC-001), a gate with no absent-state (FLW-009), a stage that breaks
pipeline purity (FLW-001), a reference to a missing template or profile, a threshold outside its
allowed range.
acceptance: AC1: `apply --validate` runs the same checks without writing and is usable in CI.
AC2: A partially valid bundle applies nothing.
requirements.source: meta-harness tradition of script refusals (DESIGN §3.6 "prose rule → script refusal"); `repos_check.py`.

requirements.title: See the effect before saving
requirements.statement:
Changing a policy, lane or project setting shows a diff and a what-if: how the Pickup Preview
would differ.
acceptance: AC1: The what-if uses the scheduler's own evaluator with the proposed values.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 view 7 (simulate); UI-008.

requirements.title: A default bundle ships with every release
requirements.statement:
Each release carries a default bundle: the `change` and `job` workflows, their packet templates,
the review checklists, harness profiles for the shipped harnesses, and default policies. A fresh
install applies it. On upgrade, changed defaults are offered as a diff the operator accepts; an
installation's edits are never overwritten.
acceptance: AC1: A fresh install can run the demo with no definition authored by the user.
AC2: An upgrade never changes behaviour by silently replacing a definition the operator edited.
requirements.source: `definitions/seed/` (9 workflows, 4 roles, 2 archetypes, 4 context recipes, 8 lanes, 10 policies — to be re-cut to the kinds in DEF-001); CORPUS M1.2.

requirements.title: Onboarding a project is one object and one check
requirements.statement:
A project is onboarded by creating it with its repositories, lanes, build and release switches.
An onboarding check then verifies and reports: the landing credential can push; auto-merge is
allowed; at least one required check exists (or the plain-git adapter is chosen); the mirror is
created. Claims start only when the check passes.
acceptance: AC1: A project whose check fails shows exactly which item failed and stays unbuilt.
AC2: Onboarding needs no edit to any file outside Sortyard.
requirements.source: onboarding.md (one `repos.yaml` entry; the onboarding check; "GitHub requirements per repo"); SY-DEC-003 (registration sequence: build registry first, driver last).

requirements.title: Three ways to extend, none of them in-process
requirements.statement:
Sortyard is extended by (1) **definitions** applied as bundles, (2) **containers** that honour a
published contract (worker images, sensors), and (3) **HTTP** (the API, MCP, the event stream,
webhooks). 1.0 loads no third-party code into the control plane and has no plugin registry.
acceptance: AC1: The architecture page lists every extension point with its contract version.
AC2: A change that would require third-party code inside the API or controller process is out of scope for 1.0.
requirements.source: DESIGN §11.1 ("Small core, everything else an extension"); CF-05 for why the six-kind registry and SDK are cut.

requirements.title: Worker image contract and conformance kit
requirements.statement:
The stage contract (EXE-006) is published with a conformance kit: a container that plays the
controller's side against a candidate worker image and reports pass or fail per clause. The
shipped harness images pass it in CI.
acceptance: AC1: A third party can build a harness image and verify it with one command and no Sortyard install.
requirements.source: CORPUS M5.7 (conformance test kit); EXE-012.

requirements.title: Git host adapters
requirements.statement:
Everything Sortyard needs from a Git host is one interface: fetch, push a branch, open or update
a change request, read its state and checks, arm and disarm auto-merge, comment, read protection
rules, mint a read-only token. 1.0 ships `plain-git` and `github`.
acceptance: AC1: The scenario suite is written against the interface and runs on both a fake and `plain-git`.
AC2: A capability an adapter lacks is declared, and dependent features say so (plain-git has no hosted checks, so CIH features are inactive).
requirements.source: DESIGN §5.2 ("GitHub Issues and Linear … integrations, never dependencies"); AGENTS.md "pipeline purity".

requirements.title: Sensors are scheduled jobs that call the API
requirements.statement:
A sensor is a container run on a schedule by the same Job machinery as stages, in its own lane
outside the delivery pipeline, with a sensor token. It files findings and heartbeats through the
API. Sensors may reach live systems; delivery stages may not.
acceptance: AC1: A sensor's schedule is a registered mechanism with a freshness window (REC-017).
AC2: A finding is de-duplicated by a stable key: repeats update its last-seen time.
requirements.source: DESIGN §3.7 (Sensor), §1.4; factory-measurement-contract ("repeat sweeps update age instead of duplicating incidents").

requirements.title: Bundles from a repository at a pinned ref
requirements.statement:
`apply` accepts a Git URL and a commit or tag; the bundle's source and content hash are recorded
on every version it creates.
acceptance: AC1: An unpinned ref (a branch name) is refused unless explicitly allowed.
requirements.source: DESIGN §3.7 (registry "git-backed in v1"); CORPUS M3.2.

requirements.title: Tracker import adapters
requirements.statement:
Importing from an external tracker is an interface with one shipped implementation (Plane):
list projects, items, relations, states, order and comments read-only.
acceptance: AC1: The adapter holds a read-only credential and issues only read requests (asserted by the HTTP fake).
requirements.source: `src/sortyard/shadow/sources.py` (GET only; refuses redirects that would carry the key elsewhere); MIG-003.

requirements.title: Contracts are versioned
requirements.statement:
The stage contract, the adapter interfaces and the bundle format carry versions. A release
states which versions it supports; a contract version is supported for at least two minor
releases after its successor ships.
acceptance: AC1: A worker image built for the previous contract version still runs on the current release.
requirements.source: DESIGN §11.2 ("an API-stability/versioning commitment").

requirements.title: One chart, one image, three control-plane workloads
requirements.statement:
One Helm chart and one image. Control-plane workloads: `api` (HTTP, console, MCP), `controller`
(scheduler, chain advancement, mirrors, schedules, health checks) and `integrator` (Git host
writes). Workers are Jobs. MS1 installs `api` and Postgres; `controller` and `integrator` join in
MS3. A single-pod profile for evaluation may run all three in one pod.
acceptance: AC1: The default install renders at most: three Deployments, one StatefulSet (bundled Postgres), their Services, Secrets, ConfigMaps, NetworkPolicies and one migration Job.
AC2: The eval-runner, sensor-runner and context-assembler stub services in the repo are removed (CF-10).
requirements.source: SY-DEC-001 (one codebase, entry points, all-in-one profile); DESIGN §4 (six services); CF-10. Plane benchmark: 13 containers.

requirements.title: Installable by a namespace admin
requirements.statement:
The chart needs no CustomResourceDefinitions and no cluster-scoped objects by default. Optional
cluster-scoped extras (a PriorityClass, a second namespace for workers) are flags, each
documented with what is lost without it.
acceptance: AC1: `helm install` succeeds with a ServiceAccount that has admin on one namespace only.
AC2: From MS3, when the controller ships: its Role is limited to Jobs, Pods, Pods/log, ConfigMaps and Secrets in the worker namespace.
requirements.source: 2026-11-12 release stall (a new CronJob could not be applied because a hand-maintained Role did not name it); `k8s/mh-rbac.yaml`.

requirements.title: Postgres and one blob location, nothing else
requirements.statement:
State, ledger and work queue are in Postgres. Blobs (packets, logs, traces, mirrors) go to a blob
store with two backends: a PersistentVolume (default) or S3-compatible storage. There is no
Redis, no message broker and no required object store.
acceptance: AC1: The default install has exactly one database and one PersistentVolumeClaim besides Postgres's own.
AC2: Switching the blob backend is a values change plus a documented copy step.
requirements.source: SY-DEC-001 ("Postgres is the only database … no Redis, no message broker"); DESIGN §4 storage choices (which adds an S3 store — see CF-11).

requirements.title: Bundled or external Postgres
requirements.statement:
The chart can run Postgres for evaluation or use an existing server. Supported major versions
are stated (16 and 17 at 1.0) and tested in CI. Production guidance says to use an external,
backed-up Postgres.
acceptance: AC1: The install test runs against both modes.
AC2: A wrong credential fails readiness (API-014).
requirements.source: README quickstart (`postgres.enabled=false`); goldfish GF1-07.

requirements.title: Install time
requirements.statement:
From a clean kind cluster with the prerequisites present: a running Sortyard with the first task
filed in at most 15 minutes (MS1); the demo chain finished in at most 30 minutes (MS3). Both are
scripted and timed in CI on every release candidate, using published artefacts only.
acceptance: AC1: The CI job fails when either bar is exceeded on the reference runner.
AC2: The documented path has at most 8 commands and no step that requires editing a file.
requirements.source: DESIGN §1.9 ("`helm install` it on a fresh cluster in an afternoon") — tightened; goldfish GF1-05 (no prerequisite check, no one-command replica).

requirements.title: Values are few, documented and schema-checked
requirements.statement:
The chart ships a `values.schema.json`; every value has a comment and a default; a default
install requires no values. The values reference page is generated.
acceptance: AC1: `helm install` with an unknown or mistyped value fails with the schema's message.
AC2: Fewer than 10 values need a decision for a production install; they are listed on one page.
requirements.source: `charts/sortyard/values.yaml`; Plane benchmark (58 variables in the self-host env file).

requirements.title: Migrations
requirements.statement:
Numbered, forward-only SQL migrations, each applied in one transaction with its record; a
released migration is immutable and the runner refuses a changed file. The migration Job runs
**before** new application pods start (a pre-upgrade hook; post-install on first install).
Migrations follow expand-then-contract so the previous application version keeps working on the
new schema. The runner refuses to run against a schema newer than the release knows.
acceptance: AC1: CI applies every migration to a database at the previous release's schema while the previous release's test suite runs against it.
AC2: Each release documents whether its migrations are online-safe and their expected duration on the reference data set.
requirements.source: `charts/sortyard/migrations/migrate.sh` (immutability check); `templates/migrations.yaml` (currently `post-install,post-upgrade`); Plane benchmark (a migrator container and a migration check workflow).

requirements.title: Upgrade guarantees
requirements.statement:
From 1.0: any 1.x upgrades directly to any later 1.y; this is tested in CI from the last patch
of every earlier minor, with data. Rolling back the application by one minor without restoring
the database is supported. Before 1.0: each 0.x upgrades from 0.(x−1), tested, with any
exception in the upgrade notes.
acceptance: AC1: The upgrade matrix job seeds data with the old version, upgrades, and runs the new version's scenario suite.
AC2: Every release has upgrade notes even when they say "nothing to do".
requirements.source: CORPUS M6.3; Plane benchmark (an upgrade option in `setup.sh` and a one-off `migration-0.13-0.14.sh`; no stated guarantee found in the repo).

requirements.title: Work in flight survives upgrades and restarts
acceptance: AC1: Upgrade during 20 running chains: all complete with no extra attempt caused by the upgrade.
requirements.source: conductor README "API rollouts" (strategy Recreate leaves 30–40 s with nothing listening; 11 rollouts in a day failed reviews and grooming).

requirements.title: Availability during upgrade
requirements.statement:
The API rolls without downtime with two replicas; the controller and integrator hand over
leadership within 60 seconds. With one replica each, the documented gap is under 60 seconds and
harmless (REC-016).
acceptance: AC1: A continuous read probe during upgrade sees no failed request with two API replicas.
requirements.source: `k8s/deployment.yaml` (`replicas: 1`, `strategy: Recreate` because of a single-writer SQLite database).

requirements.title: Backup and restore
requirements.statement:
Documented and scripted backup of the database and blobs (`sortyardctl backup create`), and
restore into a fresh install. A restore drill runs in CI: back up a seeded install, restore
elsewhere, run the scenario suite's read checks.
acceptance: AC1: The restored install has identical ledger sequence and content hashes.
AC2: The docs state the recovery point for each backup method.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark (backup option and `restore.sh`, `restore-airgapped.sh` scripts); DESIGN §6 view 12.

requirements.title: Uninstall is documented
requirements.statement:
The docs say exactly what survives `helm uninstall` (the database Secret and volume) and how to
remove it.
acceptance: AC1: The uninstall section is exercised by the install test.
requirements.source: goldfish GF1-08.

requirements.title: Footprint
requirements.statement:
An idle control plane with bundled Postgres requests at most 0.5 CPU and 1 GiB of memory in
total.
acceptance: AC1: The chart test sums the default requests and fails above the bar.
requirements.source: `values.yaml` today (API 50m/64Mi, Postgres 100m/256Mi); Plane benchmark (minimum 2 vCPU / 4 GB).

requirements.title: Pod security and network policy
requirements.statement:
Every Sortyard pod runs as non-root with a read-only root filesystem, no added capabilities and
the default seccomp profile, and passes the Kubernetes `restricted` pod security standard — the
only exception being the opt-in container sidecar (EXE-016). The chart ships NetworkPolicies:
the API is reachable only from the ingress and Sortyard's own pods; workers reach only what
EXE-005 lists.
acceptance: AC1: The chart test validates manifests against the `restricted` standard.
AC2: A pod in another namespace cannot reach the API port when policies are enforced.
requirements.source: `Dockerfile` (`USER 10001`); `k8s/networkpolicy.yaml` (`control-plane-ingress-node-only`); HC02-BACKEND-LOCKDOWN-DESIGN; Plane benchmark (no `USER` directive in its API, web and live Dockerfiles).

requirements.title: Air-gapped install
requirements.statement:
The control plane needs no outbound network at runtime beyond the configured Git host and model
provider. The release lists every image by digest; worker images can have agent CLIs baked in so
that nothing is downloaded at stage start.
acceptance: AC1: The install test passes with a registry mirror and no other egress.
requirements.source: DESIGN §4 ("Air-gapped-ish install possible"); `mh.py` worker init container installs CLIs from npm at start (notes).

requirements.title: GitOps-friendly
requirements.statement:
The chart renders deterministically, keeps generated secrets stable across upgrades, and works
under Argo CD and Flux, including its migration hook.
acceptance: AC1: `helm template` twice gives identical output; an Argo CD sync of the chart in CI ends Healthy and Synced.
requirements.source: DESIGN §4 ("GitOps-friendly"); `postgres-secret.yaml` (password kept across upgrades).

requirements.title: Supported Kubernetes versions
requirements.statement:
Each release states the Kubernetes minors it supports (the current and two previous at release
time) and CI runs the install and demo on each, on kind and on k3s.
acceptance: AC1: The matrix is in the release notes and the CI configuration.
requirements.source: the estate runs k3s; the quickstart uses kind.

requirements.title: One-command local replica
requirements.statement:
One command on a machine with Docker checks prerequisites and their versions, creates a local
cluster, builds and loads the image, installs the chart in the deployment's own shape, and
prints how to reach it. The same environment runs the scenario suite.
acceptance: AC1: A zero-context agent goes from a fresh clone to a passing `verify` with two commands.
AC2: The replica uses the scripted harness and the plain-git adapter; it needs no account anywhere.
requirements.source: goldfish GF1-05; CORPUS M1.1; AGENTS.md "Local-first delivery" (the local replica is the deployment shape); SORTYARD-13 (open).

requirements.title: Multi-architecture images
requirements.statement: Images are published for `amd64` and `arm64`.
acceptance: AC1: The demo passes on an arm64 kind cluster in CI.
requirements.source: inference (contributors on Apple-silicon laptops).

requirements.title: A release has one identity
requirements.statement:
Chart version, image tag and application version are tied; the image is referenced by digest in
the rendered manifests of a release; `/v1/info` and the console footer show version, commit and
digest.
acceptance: AC1: The quickstart never asks the reader to build an image or match a tag by hand.
requirements.source: README quickstart (build locally, "the tag must match `appVersion`"); goldfish "Not verified: whether the image is published"; k3s driver (digest annotations on the deployment).

requirements.title: Sizing guidance
requirements.statement:
The docs give cap and envelope defaults by node size, with the reasoning, starting from the
estate's experience.
acceptance: AC1: The guidance includes a worked example for a 16 vCPU / 64 GiB node.
requirements.source: DESIGN §3.7b (proof-class sizing on D8s_v6 versus D16s_v6); driver §5.

requirements.title: Freeze the legacy evidence now
requirements.statement:
Before any legacy component changes because of Sortyard: capture the control-plane ledger, the
scorecard battery corpus and baselines, and a Plane export; hash them; publish the manifest
digest.
acceptance: AC1: `legacy_evidence.py verify` passes on the snapshot, and its digest is recorded on the tracking item.
AC2: This is the first item worked in MS0.
requirements.source: `legacy-evidence/README.md`; CORPUS M1.15 ("the only corpus item that becomes impossible later"). Status 2026-11-12: the tool is merged (SORTYARD-11 Done) but no snapshot exists; the capture items SORTYARD-70 and SORTYARD-71 are still Todo.

requirements.title: Record the legacy conductor's inputs, pass by pass
requirements.statement:
The legacy conductor's per-pass inputs (board view, project configuration, gating output) and
its claims are retained with the legacy revision that produced them, as a replay corpus.
acceptance: AC1: At least 7 consecutive days are retained before MS2's comparison, and retention continues until the last cutover.
AC2: Each recorded pass names the legacy bundle digest it ran on.
requirements.source: README "Shadow conductor" (pass feed; "A pass with no retained inputs can only be read live while it is the newest"); CORPUS R5 (the baseline moves); SORTYARD-79 (still Todo).

requirements.title: Plane importer
requirements.statement:
Import one Plane project into a Sortyard project: tasks with their spec blocks parsed into typed
fields, parents, blocked-by relations, states, manual order, priorities, due dates, notes, and
the control labels mapped to typed fields (TRK-009). A dry run prints an object-class difference
report and changes nothing.
acceptance: AC1: For each driven board, the dry-run report shows zero unmapped control labels and zero dropped relations.
AC2: The eligible set and its order after import equal the legacy conductor's for the same instant (checked by MIG-005).
AC3: Importing twice is idempotent.
requirements.source: 2026-11-08 release note (the registers→Plane import: counts per board, 252 relations, order could not be set through Plane's API); conductor README "Plane tasks".

requirements.title: Read-only mirror mode
requirements.statement:
A Sortyard project can mirror an external board continuously and read-only. Mirrored projects
run the scheduler in observe mode only (SCH-013) and are labelled as mirrors everywhere.
acceptance: AC1: A mirrored project cannot be switched to active without the cutover action (MIG-007).
AC2: Sortyard issues no write to the mirrored tracker.
requirements.source: README "Shadow conductor" ("It never claims, merges, comments or writes anywhere but its own database").

requirements.title: Replay comparison
requirements.statement:
Run Sortyard's real evaluator over the recorded legacy passes (MIG-002) and compare claim
decisions. Every divergence is stored and classified: input difference, policy mismatch,
implementation defect, side effect the replay cannot know, or unclassified with the reason.
acceptance: AC1: Over at least 2,000 recorded passes: claim agreement of at least 99%, and 100% of divergences classified, with no open implementation defect.
AC2: The comparison is a repeatable offline job (minutes, not weeks) and runs in CI on a fixed sample.
requirements.source: `claim-comparison/README.md` (pairing, classification); DESIGN §8 Phase 1; CF-13 for replacing the live soak.

requirements.title: Migration code stays out of the core
requirements.statement:
Everything specific to the legacy estate (the Plane/`products.json`/gating adapters, the
comparator, the evidence tool, the cutover kit) lives under a `migration/` tree with its own
tests and is not imported by the `sortyard` package. The core has no NonceLogic project names,
hosts or file formats.
acceptance: AC1: An import-graph test fails if `sortyard.*` imports from `migration.*`.

AC2: A grep gate fails on estate-specific names (`noncelogic`, internal hostnames, `products.json`) in `src/`, `charts/` and the public docs. `migration/` is exempt; `docs/requirements/` is exempt until the publication step in [README.md](README.md) ("Before this directory is public").
requirements.source: `src/sortyard/shadow/` and `charts/…/shadow-conductor.yaml` are in the core today; DESIGN §1.9 ("no NonceLogic-specific assumptions in the core"); goldfish GF1-04 (internal hosts in the README).

requirements.title: Cutover kit
acceptance: AC1: The kit is first executed end to end in the replica against a copy of the project.
AC2: Running a step twice is safe.
requirements.source: CORPUS M4.1; SY-DEC-003 (the proven registration sequence).

requirements.title: One authority at a time
requirements.statement:
For any project at any moment exactly one system claims work. The kit refuses to activate a
Sortyard project while the legacy driver still has build on for it, and refuses to re-enable the
legacy driver while Sortyard is active.
acceptance: AC1: An attempt to activate with the legacy side still on fails with the evidence.
requirements.source: driver §6 ("Nothing else should build or merge for a project that has `build` on"); in-flight-steering.

requirements.title: Hypercare and rollback
requirements.statement:
Each cutover has a hypercare window (default 7 days; 14 for the pilot) with a written verdict:
claims correct, landings fenced, hand-backs owned. Until the verdict, rollback is possible: stop
Sortyard for the project, re-enable the legacy driver from the frozen snapshot. After the
verdict the legacy side for that project is switched off, not kept as a fallback.
acceptance: AC1: The rollback path is rehearsed once in the replica before the pilot.
AC2: A verdict lists every operator intervention during the window.
requirements.source: CORPUS M3.14, M4.5–M4.7; the estate's standing rule that legacy paths are shut down or cut over, never kept as a fallback.

requirements.title: Rule conformance ledger
requirements.statement:
Every enforceable rule of the legacy system is mapped to a requirement in this specification, a
policy key, a policy pack, or a recorded retirement with its reason.
[16-legacy-parity.md](16-legacy-parity.md) is the seed; it is completed against `AGENTS.md`, the
templates and the skills before the first product cutover.
acceptance: AC1: No row is left "unmapped" at the pilot's verdict.
AC2: Before each cutover, every KEEP and FIX row the project relies on has a passing parity scenario (REC-025) or a dated waiver by the owner.
requirements.source: CORPUS M5.1, M5.5 ("each prose rule either becomes a Policy or is consciously retired").

requirements.title: Legacy retirement
requirements.statement:
After the last cutover: the legacy conductor CronJobs, the dispatcher, the release controller,
the host crons and watches are removed; the Plane projects are archived read-only; final exports
are stored. A one-source-of-truth audit lists every remaining second copy of any fact; the
milestone is not done while the list is non-empty.
acceptance: AC1: Each retired watch or cron names the Sortyard mechanism that replaces it, or the reason it is no longer needed.
requirements.source: CORPUS M4.8–M4.10; MECHANISMS.md registry (the list of what exists).

requirements.title: Estate mechanism observers
requirements.statement:
The estate mechanisms the legacy check watches beyond the pipeline (CronJobs and resources on
three clusters, scheduled CI workflows, host timers) keep being watched: through external
heartbeats (REC-018) and an optional observer integration for cluster objects and CI schedules.
acceptance: AC1: Before the legacy mechanism check is switched off, every entry of `mechanisms.yaml` is either registered in Sortyard or recorded as out of scope with an owner.
requirements.source: `mechanisms.yaml` (68 entries across HARNESS, DEVOPS, ROVE, CPV2, LOOP boards).

requirements.title: The experiment rig gets an explicit fate
requirements.statement:
The experiment rig that shares the legacy control plane (corpus, treatments, compare and eval
views, the scorecard battery) is inventoried and, by a recorded decision, either archived or kept
as its own deployment. It is not carried into Sortyard.
acceptance: AC1: The decision record exists before the legacy control plane is removed.
requirements.source: CORPUS M4.4; harness-console decided D11 (experiment views moved under "Lab").

requirements.title: Importing historical evidence
requirements.statement:
Importing the frozen ledger history and battery baselines into Sortyard is deferred. The frozen
snapshot (MIG-001) stays the record.
acceptance: AC1: Dashboards mark the period before a project's cutover as "not in Sortyard".
requirements.source: CORPUS M4.2; DESIGN §8 non-goals ("migrating historical ledger data beyond an import of open work").

requirements.title: Close out the Phase 1 prototypes
requirements.statement:
Each Phase 1 deliverable that was merged into meta-harness instead of the product repository is
either ported into `sortyard/sortyard` with its tests or recorded as retired: the identity matrix
(`identity/`), the generated clients (`clients/`), the definitions loader and seed
(`definitions/`), the claim comparator (`claim-comparison/`), the evidence tool
(`legacy-evidence/`), the latency instrument (`one-loop-latency/`), `spec/PERMISSIONS.md`.
acceptance: AC1: [14-mapping.md](14-mapping.md)'s carry-over table has a final disposition for every row.
AC2: `pytest spec` gates CI.
requirements.source: meta-harness `projects/sortyard/` (about 5,000 lines across six folders); `ci.yml` (`spec` job fails on main); board: SORTYARD-9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15 are Done while the product repo holds only PRs #1–#4.

requirements.title: The docs are a tested product surface
requirements.statement:
A docs site built from the repository, with: quickstart, install, upgrade, concepts, an
operations guide written around reason codes and absent states, troubleshooting, and generated
references (API, CLI, policy keys, reason codes, permission matrix, metrics, chart values). Every
command block in the docs is executed in CI against the replica.
acceptance: AC1: A doc command that fails breaks the build.
AC2: The generated references are never edited by hand (drift check).
AC3: The public docs contain no internal host, project or person names (grep gate, MIG-006).
requirements.source: `tests/test_readme.py` (the quickstart is already tested); goldfish GF1-04; CORPUS M6.1.

requirements.title: README
requirements.statement:
The README says what Sortyard is, shows the quickstart, links the docs, and states the project's
status honestly. Charter, tracking notes and internal references move out.
acceptance: AC1: Top to bottom, the README has no statement that contradicts another part of it.
requirements.source: goldfish GF1-04 (the charter half contradicts the top half and links internal hosts).

requirements.title: Contributor and agent guide
requirements.statement:
`AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` at the root: the architecture map, how to run the replica and
the checks, the conventions (schema-first models, domain commands, one event per change), how to
add a requirement-bearing change, and the definition of done.
acceptance: AC1: A zero-context agent lands a small, correct change using only the repository (the goldfish test for contributors), and its friction list is empty of blockers.
requirements.source: goldfish GF1-03 (no `AGENTS.md`); DESIGN §11.2; SORTYARD-13.

requirements.title: Goldfish gate at every milestone
requirements.statement:
At each milestone exit a zero-context agent, given only the public repository and docs, installs
the release candidate and performs the milestone's exit demonstration. Its findings are filed;
blockers hold the milestone. The run must happen on a machine that has the prerequisites and
network the docs assume.
acceptance: AC1: The report follows the existing format (run log, findings with severity and evidence, verdict).
AC2: Findings from the previous report are fixed, not just filed, before the next one runs.
requirements.source: `docs/goldfish/phase-1-install-smoke.md` (verdict: blocked; the cluster steps were not run because the environment had no tools or network); CORPUS R7 (the legibility thread).

requirements.title: Decision records and changelog
requirements.statement:
Architecture decisions are records with a date, an owner and a status in `DECISIONS.md` (or one
file each). `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog; every user-visible change has an entry.
acceptance: AC1: The product repository's `DECISIONS.md` contains SY-DEC-001 to SY-DEC-003 and the decisions this specification asks for (see [15-open-decisions.md](15-open-decisions.md)).
requirements.source: `DECISIONS.md` in the repo holds only SY-DEC-001; the meta-harness copy also has 002 and 003.

requirements.title: Evidence by layer
requirements.statement:
Tests sit at the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour: **domain** — one unit test per
state-machine transition and one per refused transition; **API and persistence** — contract
tests against a real Postgres: schemas, errors, authorisation, isolation, idempotency,
migrations; **UI** — component state tests and end-to-end journeys; **deploy** — one smoke per
pull request that builds the image, installs the chart on a kind cluster and expects readiness;
**scenario** — whole chains against the Git host and CI fakes with the scripted harness.
acceptance: AC1: Each layer is a named CI job and a required check.
AC2: No test sleeps on the wall clock; the clock is injected.
AC3: A test that asserts only what its fixture put in is rejected in review.
requirements.source: AGENTS.md "Testing model" (the estate's own standard, applied to Sortyard).

requirements.title: Coverage floors
requirements.statement:
Branch coverage of the domain layer at least 90%; whole backend at least 80%; console statements
at least 70% plus the journey suite. The floors only rise.
acceptance: AC1: CI fails below a floor.
requirements.source: inference — Plane publishes no coverage figure; the legacy `test_conductor.py` (10,364 lines for 2,589 of code) sets the house standard.

requirements.title: Every pull request runs everything
requirements.statement:
Lint, format, strict type-check, generated-code and generated-document drift (including this
directory's `tools/gen.py --check`), all test layers, chart lint and render, image build and the
install smoke run on every pull request and are required. No job is `continue-on-error`.
acceptance: AC1: `main` is never red: a failing required check on `main` is treated as an incident.
AC2: p95 duration of required checks is at most 15 minutes.
requirements.source: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the `spec` job is `continue-on-error`); AGENTS.md "Green main, stop the line".

requirements.title: Fork pull requests are safe to run
requirements.statement:
Pull requests from forks run the full required checks on provider-hosted runners with no
secrets and read-only permissions. Nothing in the required checks needs a secret.
acceptance: AC1: A fork pull request gets the same green or red as a branch pull request.
requirements.source: DESIGN §11.2 (fork-PR verification); `ci.yml` already uses `ubuntu-latest` with `contents: read`. The estate's "no GitHub-hosted runners" rule is about estate work and does not apply to this public repository.

requirements.title: Flaky tests are not tolerated
requirements.statement:
A test that fails intermittently is quarantined with a recorded reproduction and a task within
one day, and fixed or deleted within two weeks. Nobody re-runs to get green.
acceptance: AC1: The quarantine list is in the repository and is empty at each release.
requirements.source: AGENTS.md "Testing model" ("Never rerun just to seek a green result").

requirements.title: Scenario suite as a product asset
requirements.statement:
The scripted harness and the demo repository (MS3), and the Git host fake and the CI fake (MS4,
built with their adapters in WP4.1), are shipped and documented, so that adopters and extension
authors can test against them.
acceptance: AC1: The fakes implement the adapter interfaces (EXT-003, CIH-013) and pass the same conformance tests as the real adapters where the behaviour is defined.
requirements.source: AGENTS.md "Delivery lanes" rule 5 ("fakes encode the providers' documented behaviour").

requirements.title: Performance bars on a reference workload
requirements.statement:
On the reference workload (20 projects, 50,000 tasks, 5,000 open, 200 chains in flight): list
and detail API p95 at most 300 ms; scheduler evaluation at most 2 s per project; Overview render
at most 2 s; event-stream lag at most 2 s.
acceptance: AC1: A load job runs before each release and its results are in the release notes.
requirements.source: harness-console J1 (2 s), J2 (10,000 rows); `architecture.md` ("datasets of ~10^3–10^4 requests").

requirements.title: Security policy and response
requirements.statement:
`SECURITY.md`: private reporting channel; acknowledgement within 3 business days; a fix or
mitigation target of 30 days for high and critical; advisories published with affected versions.
acceptance: AC1: The reporting channel is tested before 1.0.
requirements.source: Plane `SECURITY.md` (three business days) — matched, with fix targets added.

requirements.title: Threat model and security review before 1.0
requirements.statement:
A written threat model covering: the permission matrix and token scopes; stage tokens and the
worker boundary; the integrator and its credential; packets carrying untrusted task text to
agents (prompt injection that tries to exfiltrate credentials or write outside the task); inbound
and outbound webhooks; the proxy-header sign-in mode. An independent adversarial review tests it;
findings are closed or accepted in writing.
acceptance: AC1: The review includes an attempt to make a worker act outside its binding and an attempt to reach another project's objects.
requirements.source: CORPUS M6.2 ("an adversarial review of the binding path"); Plane's advisory profile.

requirements.title: Dependencies are pinned and scanned
requirements.statement:
Python and JavaScript dependencies are locked with hashes. Dependency updates arrive by bot.
CodeQL, a dependency audit and a container scan run in CI; a known high or critical
vulnerability with a fix available blocks release.
acceptance: AC1: The image contains no package without a locked version.
requirements.source: `pyproject.toml` (ranges, no lock file today); Plane benchmark (CodeQL workflow, `.trivyignore`, `uv sync --locked`).

requirements.title: Signed artefacts with provenance
requirements.statement:
Each release publishes images and the chart to an OCI registry, signed (keyless), with an SBOM
and a build-provenance attestation. The docs show how to verify them, and the install test
verifies them.
acceptance: AC1: A tampered image fails verification in the install test.
requirements.source: CORPUS M6.2 ("image signing and build provenance"); the legacy release controller's digest pinning and source-ancestry checks (CI-RELEASE.md) — the guarantee is kept, the bespoke controller is not.

requirements.title: Releases come from CI, from a tag
requirements.statement:
A release is produced only by the release workflow from a signed tag on `main`. Nothing is built
on a laptop. The workflow holds no cluster credential.
acceptance: AC1: The release workflow is the only identity allowed to push release artefacts.
requirements.source: DESIGN §9 ("the reboot's own releases go through CI like everything else"); CI-RELEASE.md ("It has no Kubernetes credential or cluster network path").

requirements.title: Secrets never enter the repository
requirements.statement:
A secret scanner runs on every pull request and on history before the repository is made
public.
acceptance: AC1: The pre-publication history scan is recorded with its result.
requirements.source: the repository is private today and was seeded from an internal folder.

requirements.title: Semantic versioning with one number for app, chart and API
requirements.statement:
The application, the image and the chart share one version. Before 1.0, minors may break with
notice; from 1.0, semantic versioning applies to the API, the CLI, the chart values, the stage
contract and the database upgrade path.
acceptance: AC1: One version string is stamped into the image, the chart and the served OpenAPI document, and CI fails when they differ. What counts as breaking is defined mechanically by the compatibility jobs when they land (API-013, DEP-008, EXT-007).
requirements.source: DEP-020; `Chart.yaml` (`version` and `appVersion` both 0.1.0).

requirements.title: Release notes and upgrade notes, always
requirements.statement:
Every release has notes generated from the changelog plus an upgrade section (migrations,
duration, anything to do by hand). Each milestone ends in a tagged pre-release.
acceptance: AC1: The release workflow fails without an upgrade section.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark (release notes of 62–99 characters on some stable releases).

requirements.title: Release cadence and support window
requirements.statement: After 1.0: a minor about every six weeks; security fixes for the latest two minors.
acceptance: AC1: The policy is in `GOVERNANCE.md` and the docs.
requirements.source: inference; Plane ships about monthly.

requirements.title: Licence and contribution terms
requirements.statement:
Apache-2.0. Contributions under the Developer Certificate of Origin, checked mechanically; no
CLA. A licence scan keeps copyleft dependencies out of the distributed image. Confirmation is
the owner's (OD-1).
acceptance: AC1: A commit without sign-off fails the DCO check.
AC2: The licence scan is a required check.
requirements.source: `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0, SY-DEC-001 seed); INTENDED-USE.md standing default; DESIGN §11.5.

requirements.title: No withheld pieces
requirements.statement:
Everything needed to run Sortyard as described in its docs is in the public repository under the
project licence. There is no enterprise edition of the code.
acceptance: AC1: The docs describe no feature that the public artefacts do not contain.
requirements.source: DESIGN §11.6.

requirements.title: Governance files
requirements.statement:
`GOVERNANCE.md` (who decides, how a maintainer is added), `MAINTAINERS`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`,
issue and pull-request templates, a trademark note for the name and logo, and a public roadmap
kept as milestones in the repository's own tracker.
acceptance: AC1: The roadmap is generated from, or is, the real milestone list — not a separate page.
requirements.source: DESIGN §11.5; CORPUS M6.6.

requirements.title: Name clearance
requirements.statement:
A trademark search for "Sortyard" is completed and recorded, and the package namespaces (GitHub
organisation, PyPI, npm, container registry) are claimed, before the repository is made public.
acceptance: AC1: The record is in `DECISIONS.md`.
requirements.source: DESIGN §10 item 1 ("Still owed before public launch: a formal trademark search"; namespaces unclaimed at check time).
